blocks.text: You can add proxies to gateways and configure the Third-Party Proxy Chaining feature, which enables you to forward traffic to a third-party proxy service. The default limit for third-party proxies is 8. To increase the limit to a maximum of 255 proxies for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.
The Proxies page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Configure proxy objects (IP address or the FQDN) of a third-party proxy service that you want to integrate with the Zscaler service to provide an additional security layer for the outbound traffic.
Configure proxies that can be added to the gateways to forward specific web traffic through the third-party proxy service before reaching the destination server.

blocks.text: On the Proxies page (Internet Access > Resources > Proxies and Gateways > Proxies), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add proxies for a third-party proxy service.
Modify the table and its columns.
View a list of all proxies. For each proxy, you can view the following information:
Proxy Name: The name of the proxy. You can sort this column.
IP Address / FQDN: The IP address or the FQDN configured for this proxy.
Port: The port number configured for this proxy.
Description: Additional notes or information about the proxy.
Proxy's Root Certificate: The root certificate in this proxy which is used by Zscaler to perform SSL/TLS inspection on the traffic being forwarded by Zscaler.
Go to the DNS Gateways page.
Go to the Proxy Gateways page.
